newsitem.title: INDIA: India's BJP says nation needs new rulers.
newsitem.headline: India's BJP says nation needs new rulers.

text.p: India's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday urged President Shankar Dayal Sharma to prevent the party's rivals from forming a new government, and consider snap elections.

BJP leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee accused the United Front coalition and the Congress party of ganging up on the rightwing party out of fear of elections which could bolster the Hindu nationalists' chances of gaining power.

"The same combination which was responsible for creating the present constitutional crisis must not be allowed to rule the country under any circumstances," Vajpayee told a news conference in the northern city of Lucknow.
"It would be better to have another parliamentary election rather than allowing the same conglomeration of parties to hold the country at stake."
Vajpayee spoke on the day after caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda offered to step down as leader of the centre-left United Front coalition.
Deve Gowda's move opened the way to a possible reconciliation with Congress, which provoked his downfall on Friday by revoking support for his 10-month-old government.

Vajpayee was prime minister for 12 days last May after his party emerged from general elections as the largest single party in a hung parliament. But he was forced to step down in the face of certain defeat in a confidence vote.

The BJP is convinced that mid-term elections would put it within striking distance of a majority. The very possibility has lent impetus to efforts by the United Front and Congress to put aside their differences and strike a new power-sharing deal.
Vajpayee accused the United Front and Congress of making "patch-up efforts solely because of the fear of the BJP".
The United Front and Congress accuse the BJP of favouring India's Hindu majority at the expense of minority Moslems.
"The fact remains that both were aware that elections will benefit the BJP and therefore they were trying to gang up once again," he said.
"But it would be grossly improper to let them make yet another mockery or play another cruel joke with the nation."
Under the constitution, the president names the prime minister or calls polls. The BJP has said it would stake another claim to power only if it could be assured of a majority.
Asked whether his party would stake a claim, Vajpayee said: "That is for the president to take initiative."
In New Delhi, BJP spokesman Yashwant Sinha said it was up to the president to ensure that the current "theatre of absurdness" be ended, and that a stable government take power.
"The nation can ill afford another farce," he said.
Party spokeswoman Sushma Swaraj said any new United Front coalition backed by Congress would fall within six months.
